Instead, they choose to do this in front of the world. And my argument is that this is intentional; they want the world to hate them because by doing this, they create the ultimate taboo. If we find it disgusting and contemptuous, the entire world will unite against Israel. But guess what? That's exactly what their religion wants. In the extreme form of Jewish esquetology or their religion, they believe that at the end of the world, Israel will fight the entire world, and God will help Israel triumph in the end.

The idea of this ritual sacrifice is to unite the Israeli population. This works because when soldiers are forced into a hopeless situation with no escape, like being surrounded by flesh-eating monkeys, they unite and find strength to fight. In Chinese history, an army that retreats to a river also faces the choice between drowning or fighting to the death, leading them to unify.

So, in Gaza, there are extremists within Israel's government who want to accelerate this process of the end of the world where Israel will face the entire world. The "river" here is a taboo, such as killing children, which leaves no escape for Israel; they must either go all out or be destroyed by the world.

Online, you can see Israelis causing trouble everywhere, starting fights and shouting death to Arabs on public buses in the western world. This is intentional—to unite themselves by dividing the world.

To unpack this further, let's use a thought experiment. Imagine an island with no escape, where resources are guarded by flesh-eating monkeys. Mysteriously, 100 men from different countries and backgrounds land there. Initially, they are hopeless, but instead, they find purpose and develop a common language to fight together.

This is how the Israeli government uses sacrifice and division to unite its people and create global conflict.
